Dear Requester

The Council's Information Governance Team works collaboratively, and requests are managed collectively across the team rather than by individual officers. For this reason, correspondence is not issued under individual names. The team is managed by Evelyn Morgan who is the Council's Data Protection Officer/Information Manager.

We appreciate the detailed correspondence you have provided to date and understand that this matter is of importance to you. We have received multiple items of correspondence from you, including earlier requests relating to the legal case of BP Properties Ltd v Buckler. Work had already been undertaken to review this request and we were in the process of preparing a response when your more recent correspondence was received. We were aiming to ensure that all appropriate lines of enquiry had been explored before providing a response.

At this stage, we would like to clarify that the Vale of Glamorgan Council does not hold records relating to this historic legal matter. Neither the Council nor its predecessor authorities, the Vale of Glamorgan Borough Council or the former South Glamorgan County Council were involved in the case of BP Properties Ltd v Buckler. From the information available, it appears this was a private legal matter between BP Properties Ltd and the Buckler family. We also recognise that your enquiries extend beyond the Council and have been shared with a number of organisations. Some of the information you are seeking is more likely to be held elsewhere and not with the Council. Some information that may have historically been retained by the Council may now be held by the Glamorgan Archives but only in relation to historical land ownership, tenancy records, or court administrative deposits. Some information may also be obtainable from the Land Registry, but we can see that they have been included in your correspondence.

In terms of information the Council may hold, this is most likely limited to planning related records. As previously advised, in order for our Planning colleagues to conduct accurate searches, they have requested a copy of the relevant site plan. Without this, there is a risk that any searches undertaken may not capture all relevant records.  We note that this does not mean there are records just that in trying to cover every possibility we have asked for a site plan to complete this aspect of our enquiries.  There may not be anything held but, we are trying to search for you.  It is entirely a matter for you as to whether you provide a site plan. If you do not wish to provide one you do not have to but that will restrict our enquiries as it will be difficult to pin down the correct area.

We are looking to assist in providing you with a full response as soon as possible with the information that is held by the Council. Your cooperation in providing the requested plan will help us progress this matter efficiently.

We look forward to hearing from you.

Kind regards

Information Governance Officer / Swyddog Llywodraethu Gwybodaeth

LEGAL NOTICE TO RECIPIENTS:
Take notice that this request is issued in anticipation of formal legal proceedings and the filing of an official report regarding systemic institutional █████, land misconduct, and the unlawful concealment of historic preservation data. You are under a strict legal duty to preserve all physical and electronic records, metadata, correspondence, maps, and erased files relating to this site. Any spoliation, deletion, or withholding of data will be cited in subsequent court filings.
Dear Freedom of Information Officer,
RE: Information Request under the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and the Environmental Information Regulations 2004
I am writing to request access to historical records, internal correspondence, planning briefs, and assessments held by your organization regarding Great House Farm, Llandough, near Penarth/Cardiff (demolished December 1988), and the historical occupancy of the Buckler family.
Statutory Mandate on Accessibility & Charging Fees:
I am aware that previous attempts to locate this data have resulted in directives to visit physical archives in person or use paywalled, commercial third-party web portals. Please be advised of the following statutory obligations:

  1.  Under EIR Regulation 8, fees cannot act as an unreasonable barrier or deterrent to access. Because my family was historically displaced from this site and I am executing this request remotely, forcing physical attendance or demanding payment constitutes an unlawful obstacle.
  2.  Public authorities are required to supply information in the format requested. I require all documents to be delivered digitally via email attachment or secure electronic download link, free of charge, as specified by the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) guidelines for data already held electronically.
Please provide all recorded information matching the following points:
1. Tenant/Ownership Identification and the 1880 Report

  *   Any documents, archival notes, or registry indexes citing the William/ Buckler family line (who occupied and farmed the house across four generations).
  *   Clarification on whether my family members were formally cited as the legal owners, long-term tenants, or registered reporters of the 1880 discovery under the dining room floor.
  *   Any explicit records indicating gaps, deleted metadata, or missing volumes in your authority's archive concerning the tenancy, land-dispute maps, or agricultural heritage of Great House Farm between 1950 and 1989.
2. Statutory Protection and Cadw's Assessments

  *   Given that the site's extreme archaeological value (a 1st-to-4th-century Roman precursor villa and a massive early medieval monastic settlement) was verified by rescue operations as early as 1979, what are the recorded reasons why Cadw failed to place a statutory Schedule or Protection Order on the standing fabric of Great House Farm before its demolition?
  *   All internal correspondence, risk assessments, or ministerial briefs evaluating the preservation value of the sub-medieval direct-entry farmhouse core before it was levelled.
3. Planning Approvals and Local Authority Governance

  *   All minutes, planning committee files, and consultation responses from the local authority that granted planning permission and housing development rights on this specific acreage.
  *   Direct information explaining how the council approved planning permission for a private housing development in light of the documented historical evidence surrounding the immediate parish boundary.
4. Institutional Concealment and Historical "Ignorance"

  *   Records showing exactly where and at what stage of the planning process this archaeological evidence should have been brought up but was not, which ultimately allowed developers and public bodies to claim they were unaware of the land's deep significance until after the farmhouse was destroyed and housing development began.
  *   Any environmental impact assessments, historic environment register (HER) lookups, or developer briefs filed between 1980 and 1990 regarding the footprint of Great House Farm.
If any part of this request is refused under the guise of commercial sensitivity or archival limitations, you are required by law to state the exact statutory exemption applied and provide a formal internal review pathway.
I expect your response within the statutory 20-working-day timeframe.
Kind regards,
Requester 
█████, Vale of Glamorgan

Date(s)

I hope you find this information useful.

Yours sincerely,

Hannah Price

Hi Mike,

Appreciate the reply.

I kindly request an internal review of the response provided under ATISN
27021.

I am grateful for the release of the two inspection photographs dated 29
July 1988. However, I am not satisfied that the searches undertaken were
sufficient to establish that no other relevant records are held or can be
accounted for.

The response states that Great House Farm was visited and assessed for
listing by Cadw inspectors, but that the only surviving records are two
photographs. It further states that any associated records may have been
transferred to the Royal Commission on the Ancient and Historical Monuments
of Wales or destroyed under the Public Records Act 1958.

I respectfully submit that this conclusion appears difficult to reconcile
with the contemporary evidence.

Contemporary newspaper reports from December 1988 record that:

Cadw was actively considering emergency listing ("spot-listing") procedures
in relation to Great House Farm;

Cadw inspectors visited the site;
Cadw assessed the architectural and archaeological significance of the
property;
Cadw communicated a decision that the building did not warrant statutory
protection.

These activities would ordinarily be expected to generate records such as
inspection notes, recommendations, assessments, correspondence, memoranda,
listing files, briefing notes, internal communications, or decision records.

In addition, a surviving family witness who was present during the
inspection recalls that a written assessment was produced and supplied to
the family. The witness recalls that the assessment concluded that,
although the site was old, the building had undergone substantial
alteration over the centuries and was therefore not considered sufficiently
significant for listing.

This █████ appears broadly consistent with the reasoning attributed
to Cadw in contemporary press reports.
I therefore request clarification of the following:

Were searches undertaken for inspection notes, site notes, assessment
reports, recommendations, listing files, briefing papers, internal
memoranda, correspondence, and decision records relating to Great House
Farm?
Were accession records, transfer schedules, disposal schedules, or archive
catalogues searched to determine whether such records once existed?

If records were transferred to RCAHMW, please identify any transfer
references, accession numbers, file references, or other metadata recording
that transfer.
If records were destroyed, please identify the disposal authority,
retention schedule, and date of destruction.

If no written assessment, recommendation, report, or decision record ever
existed, please explain how Cadw reached and communicated conclusions
regarding the architectural and archaeological significance of the property.

I am not seeking reconsideration of the 1988 listing decision itself.
Rather, I seek clarification regarding the apparent absence of records
relating to a matter that was publicly reported at the time as being under
active consideration by Cadw and which resulted in a communicated decision.

Thank you for undertaking an internal review.

Yours faithfully,

Requester

Buckler family association with the property

to the property
Any relevant material in the Bute Estate collection connected to land
transactions affecting the site

catalogue references / classmarks for relevant material held in your
collections.

through your catalogue system.

replica of Great House Farm. Any assistance from my community back there
would be appreciated, as this is a massive undertaking.

Thank you for your assistance.

Kind regards,

Requester

Dear Requester,

I have undertaken a reasonable search of our records and would advise 
you as follows:

a) The minutes of all council minutes for the period in question were 
deposited in the Glamorgan Records Office in 2002. These cover the 
period from 1982 when Llandough Community Council was first formed. 
Prior to that time, the community of Llandough was included in the remit 
of Penarth Town Council. The relevant web-link which shows the 
information held is : perihttps://glamarchives.gov.uk/od

b) You are able to visit the Glamorgan Records Office in Cardiff by 
appointment and the web-link to find details of their location is: 
https://glamarchives.gov.uk/

Section 21 of the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) is an absolute 
exemption that allows public authorities to refuse a request if the 
requested information is already reasonably accessible to the applicant 
by other means. This avoids duplicating effort and prevents authorities 
from acting as personal research services.

c) I would suggest that you access the Llandough Community Council's 
website for historical information about the community of Llandough - 
web-link is :

https://www.llandough-cc.co.uk/Buildings_of_Significance_in_our_Community_25590.aspx

Kind regards,

Paul R. Egan BA, Chartered MCIPD, CiLCA, F. Inst. LM, FIPSM

Thank you for your response and for confirming that the Council's minute

accessible through Glamorgan Archives. I shall pursue those records
directly with the archive.

Ty Mawr (Great House Farm), Llandough;
the associated farm lands;
the Williams family;
Billy Buckler, [member of the public] and members of the Buckler family;
BP Properties Ltd v Buckler and related matters.

Accordingly, I would be grateful if you could clarify:

Whether the Council presently holds any records responsive to the above
request other than the deposited minute books;
If such records exist, whether they remain in the Council's possession or
were transferred to another archive or repository;
If no such records are held, whether this is because they were never
created, were transferred elsewhere, or were subsequently destroyed;
Whether the Council retains any record of Billy Buckler addressing the
Council, whether in minutes, correspondence, agenda papers, clerk's notes
or any other form.

For the avoidance of doubt, I am content to receive a simple confirmation
of whether such records are held and their location, rather than requiring
the Council to undertake extensive historical research.

Thank you for your assistance and I look forward to hearing from you.

Yours sincerely,

Requester
